Brendan McDermid/Reuters



Anxiety about the Iran war, inflation and mushrooming public debt have driven the recent selloff in Treasury bonds. There is another factor that could add volatility into the mix:  hedge funds, a growing force in this market. [https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/bond-markets-hedge-funds-003c6ea8]

For decades, governments could rely on predictable buy-and-hold investors to snap up their sovereign debt. Now, pensions and other long-run investors are pulling back in search of higher returns elsewhere, leaving a void filled by hedge funds and other faster-twitch traders.

Hedge funds held about $2 trillion of Treasurys at the start of this year, more than double their holdings five years earlier, according to the Treasury Department’s Office of Financial Research, which said hedge funds controlled a record 7% of the market. Data released by the Federal Reserve on Friday suggests that funds’ Treasury holdings remain elevated, says Molly Brooks, a research strategist at TD Securities.

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

Planning & Investing               Bond Yields Could Come Down as Fast as They’ve Climbed

Expectations for what the Fed will do  are driving the recent moves in long-term yields. [https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/bond-yields-could-come-down-as-fast-as-theyve-climbed-d64ea9cd]

Market Talk               

From  Dow Jones Newswires [https://www.dowjones.com/professional/newswires/]



Investors should focus on the vote split at the Bank of England rate decision on Thursday for a signal on the possibility of a BOE interest-rate increases in future months, Peel Hunt's Kallum Pickering says in a note. Additionally, communication by monetary policy committee members could provide clues, he says. If BOE Governor Andrew Bailey doubles down on his comments about second-round inflation effects being subdued, this could lower expectations of BOE rate increases, Pickering says. However, if the governor indicates higher inflation expectations then markets will see that as an endorsement of current market pricing, he says. Investors fully price in a total of four BOE rate increases by mid-2027, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

A total of 79% of fund managers polled in Bank of America's global fund manager survey for September say they don't expect any of the AI companies to announce a cut in capital expenditure this year. This is up from 71% of fund managers in the August survey. Only 14% of respondents said they expect an AI capex reduction this year, BofA says. The survey was conducted between Sept. 4 and Sept. 10, before Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk, chief executives at massive AI companies, called for a slowdown in AI development. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

Barron's Advisor               The Office Boom Is Back. Can REITs Be Far Behind?

With many employees back at their desks, it’s now investors’ turn to start planning their return  to beaten-down real estate investment trusts. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/office-boom-back-reits-commercial-real-estate-ff8627a2?mod=hp_SP_A_5_1]

Business & Practice               Oil Executives Say the Great Fuel Crisis Is Here

Trump officials say the oil-market disruption is temporary, but Chevron’s Mike Wirth and others warn global supplies  are running low, with no respite in sight [https://www.wsj.com/business/energy-oil/oil-executives-say-the-great-fuel-crisis-is-here-b6b32030?mod=business_lead_pos2]

Impact Investing               As AI Filters Into Cybersecurity, Companies Seek Out Seasoned Workers

More experienced workers are being recruited to face off against supercharged AI hackers. But industry watchers  fear a coming ‘talent chasm’ if younger workers aren’t brought along. [https://www.wsj.com/pro/cybersecurity/as-ai-filters-into-cybersecurity-companies-seek-out-seasoned-workers-408af3b3]

Talking Points               Warsh’s Arrival Ended Trump’s War With the Fed. A Rate Hike Would Test the Truce.

The current Fed chairman criticized the central bank last year for moving too slowly to cut rates. Investors now expect him to start taking those cuts back,  seven weeks before the midterms. [https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/warshs-arrival-ended-trumps-war-with-the-fed-a-rate-hike-would-test-the-truce-8fd9058f]

Travel & Lifestyle               A Snooty Sport Gets a Scottish Makeover—With Beer, Sand and Dogs on the Pitch            

Jeff J Mitchell/Getty Images



Cricket, long regarded in the U.K. as the game of the upper classes, is experiencing a revival— without some of its famously haughty traditions. [https://www.wsj.com/sports/sand-beer-and-dogs-on-the-pitch-scots-are-suddenly-crazy-about-cricket-f5587525?mod=lifestyle_feat1_travel_pos2]
